candidate.headline: Pega CSSA · event-driven Kafka integration · Service-REST replay & dead-letter recovery · metadata-driven JSON mapping · Pega observability
proofPoints: Batch-to-real-time Kafka ingestion across 50+ topics, millions of records, seven APAC markets
Multi-hour batch runs cut to under 15 minutes
Service-REST replay + dead-letter recovery: incident recovery from ~2 hours to under 2 minutes
Runtime metadata-driven JSON mapping: new-format onboarding from ~4 weeks to ~10 minutes
$250K+ annual savings from automation (hub profile figure)
candidate.honesty: Production depth is integration, case management and observability. CDH strategy design is not production experience, so position for the data and integration side of decisioning teams.

tiers.name: High-Throughput & Event-Driven
tiers.evidence: Job descriptions and talks name Kafka, events and async patterns (CBA/ASB JD), externalised Kafka on OpenShift (Cisco PegaWorld 2025), Kafka/JMS (First Citizens SE II JD), Kafka/async plus queue processors on WaaS 24.1.3 (Wells Fargo), payment investigations at SWIFT/Fed volume (Wells, Goldman, JPMC), sanctions screening (BNY), 8M+ invoices across 40+ countries (Siemens CCMT) and real-time agent data for ~10,000 agents (Booking).
friction: Consumer lag and backpressure when topic volume outpaces queue processors or data flows; node scaling is reactive.
Replays create duplicate cases or double writebacks because handlers are not idempotent.
Poison messages are handled by hand, so a bad payload turns into a multi-hour incident with log digging.
Schema drift across markets/versions breaks hard-coded mappings at every rollout.
No end-to-end trace from topic offset to case ID to downstream writeback, so support cannot prove where an event died.
Re-platforming (OpenShift, Pega Cloud, active-passive DR) changes rebalancing and failover behaviour of consumers.
talkingPoints: Throughput without fragility: I moved batch integrations to real-time Kafka ingestion across 50+ topics and seven markets. Multi-hour batch windows came down to under 15 minutes, and handlers are idempotent, so replays never create duplicate cases.

Recovery as a feature, not a runbook: I built Service-REST replay and dead-letter handling that parks failed events with case context and reprocesses them automatically. Incident recovery went from ~2 hours to under 2 minutes, with monitoring that ties offset → case → writeback.

tiers.name: Decisioning & Intelligence
tiers.evidence: Public sources: ~200 adaptive models at ~200 ms decisions (CBA), 1,800 NBA actions across 8 channels and a Pega Cloud migration started because of timeouts (NatWest), 10+ channels for 6.4M customers (VOIS), a Bengaluru decisioning-architect hiring wave in 2025–26 (Standard Chartered), Process AI in case management (Telstra), and CDH/ML product teams (Pegasystems).
friction: Real-time event ingestion into CDH (Kafka data sets, data flows) cannot keep up with decision SLAs, so NBA runs on stale context.
Response capture at volume: late or missing responses starve adaptive models.
Validating strategy changes at scale before production (one public post notes teams without BOE fall back on manual testing).
Cloud migration and upgrade stability: timeouts, long upgrade cycles, data-flow tuning.
Onboarding each new channel or data source needs mapping code and a release.
talkingPoints: The data path into decisioning: real-time NBA usually fails on ingestion, not strategy (late, malformed or duplicate events). I build high-throughput Kafka ingestion with dead-letter handling and lag monitoring, so decisions run on current context.

Configurable onboarding: my metadata-driven JSON mapping layer cut new-source onboarding from ~4 weeks to ~10 minutes. For a CDH team, new channels or attributes can be wired by configuration, without a release. I'd pair with your decisioning architects rather than claim strategy-design depth.

tiers.name: Core Case Management & Enterprise Modernisation
companies: Nike / Levi's / Intel / GE HealthCare / Unilever and other Tier-B/C teams
tiers.evidence: Pega 24.x with Constellation and 24/7 production support (Empower), legacy rebuilt in 14 weeks on Blueprint/Pega Cloud (DTICI), order orchestration and DevOps (Nokia), Infinity + Constellation + GenAI JDs (Broadridge), migration/modernisation of banking apps (Société Générale), BT Business platform modernisation (BT), KYC/onboarding platforms (Morgan Stanley), on-prem 8.8 with FileNet (MUFG).
friction: Legacy retirement: mapping old system-of-record formats into Pega data models, with reconciliation done in spreadsheets.
Upgrades (8.x → 24/25) and Constellation re-platforming expose custom UI and guardrail debt.
Writeback to systems of record fails silently, leaving cases and SOR out of sync until a support ticket arrives.
Background processing (file listeners, job schedulers, BIX extracts) grows into long nightly runs and on-call load.
Contractor-heavy maintenance concentrates knowledge in vendors.
talkingPoints: Batch retirement during modernisation: I replaced file/batch integrations with Kafka and REST, taking multi-hour runs to under 15 minutes and removing a nightly support burden. It's the kind of change that makes a re-platformed app cheaper to run, not just newer.

Self-healing writebacks and configurable mapping: failed SOR updates land in a replay/dead-letter queue with case context and recover automatically (~2 hours → under 2 minutes), and metadata-driven mapping makes new legacy formats a configuration task (weeks → minutes).

scripts.useFor: Cisco, Wells Fargo, Siemens, John Deere, First Citizens peers
scripts.text: Hi [Name] — your [Cisco] team's move to externalised Kafka during the OpenShift migration is close to what I work on: high-throughput Kafka ingestion into Pega across 50+ topics. The hard part for us wasn't throughput, it was replay and dead-letter handling: making reprocessing idempotent so a failover doesn't create duplicate cases. How does your team handle reprocessing after a consumer rebalance — replay from offsets, or park failures in a recovery queue? Happy to share what worked for us; it took recovery from about two hours to under two minutes. — Sathvik, Pega CSSA

scripts.useFor: Standard Chartered, NatWest, VOIS, Verizon, CBA decisioning peers
scripts.text: Hi [Name] — your work on [CDH / NBA at Standard Chartered] caught my attention. I work on the ingestion side of Pega: Kafka events feeding a metadata-driven JSON mapping layer, so new sources onboard without code changes. In the setups I've seen, real-time NBA quality depends more on late or malformed events and response capture than on strategies. Is that your experience, or does the bottleneck sit elsewhere — data flows, simulation, model feedback? I'd value your view and can share what we learned about event plumbing. — Sathvik, Pega CSSA

Multi-hour runs ended up under 15 minutes. How is your team handling background processing and SOR writeback in the new build — queue processors, listeners, something else? Curious how it compares. — Sathvik, Pega CSSA

I ask because my strength is the integration side of that problem: Kafka ingestion, configurable data mapping and monitoring so decisions run on current data. If expansion is planned in Bengaluru, I'd appreciate knowing where to keep an eye out. — Sathvik D N, Pega CSSA

Hi [Name] — I enjoyed reading about [the 14-week Blueprint rebuild / your platform modernisation]. Will the next phase stay with the current team, or is the Bengaluru team expanding for it? I'm a Pega CSSA whose work is the unglamorous part of modernisation: retiring batch integrations, making SOR writebacks self-recovering, and making data mapping configurable. If that's on your roadmap, I'd welcome a pointer to the right team when the time comes. — Sathvik D N

Find one dated, public change: a migration, upgrade, Blueprint/Constellation rebuild, cloud move, new squad or new manager. Use it as the first line of every message. No hook means no message yet.

Peer (same band, recent joiner) → architect/lead (one technical question) → manager only with a role ID → leadership only for roadmap questions. Never message two people on the same squad on the same day. If you are in an active interview loop, message peers only.

Derive the three likeliest deep-dive questions from that firm's JD and workstreams (not hearsay): usually one integration/resilience design, one platform/version question (Cloud, Constellation, upgrade) and one domain case-design question. Prepare a 3-minute whiteboard answer for each.

Contractor or staffing-firm seats posing as direct roles, '24/7 support' or 'BAU' wording, title inflation through consulting titles, Pega being replaced by Java/low-code alternatives, frozen or removed postings, and the lead or decision-makers sitting in another city.
